chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the Imam delivers the sermon on Friday, it is not appropriate for anyone to speak until the Imam finishes his sermon. When he finishes the Imam finishes his sermon, they may speak until the prayer is established. Whether he hears the recitation or not, it is sufficient for him."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on speaking during and after the Friday sermon in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal boundaries of the Friday sermon etiquette, distinguishing between the mandatory silence during the Imam's address and the permissible discourse in the interval before the prayer. It highlights the scholarly consensus that the validity of the sermon is not contingent upon the congregation's auditory perception, but rather on the Imam's completion of the delivery, emphasizing the structural integrity of the congregational ritual.
